The framework supports multiple AI coding platforms including Claude Code, Cursor, and others through plugin marketplaces or manual installation.

It helps developers understand codebases faster by extracting and visualizing relationships between components, architectural decisions, and design rationale across multiple file types. The tool uses a two-pass approach combining deterministic AST parsing with Claude-powered concept extraction, requiring 71.5x fewer tokens per query compared to reading raw files.

It automatically scores job opportunities using a weighted A-F system across 10 dimensions, generates ATS-optimized PDFs tailored to specific job descriptions, and scrapes job portals in batch to maintain a centralized pipeline dashboard. The system is designed to be customized by Claude itself, allowing users to modify scoring criteria, company lists, and evaluation frameworks through natural language requests.

repos.description: A theoretical reconstruction of the Claude Mythos architecture, built from first principles using the available research literature.
repos.blurb: OpenMythos is a theoretical reconstruction of Claude's Mythos architecture implemented as a Recurrent-Depth Transformer (RDT) that loops a subset of transformer layers multiple times per forward pass. It enables compute-adaptive reasoning by allowing variable loop iterations during inference, potentially improving systematic generalization without generating intermediate tokens. The implementation uses input injection at each loop iteration to prevent hidden state drift and includes switchable attention mechanisms (MLA/GQA) with sparse MoE layers.

repos.blurb: Boneyard is a TypeScript framework that automatically generates pixel-perfect skeleton loading screens by extracting DOM element positions from your actual components. It eliminates the need to manually create placeholder layouts by using `getBoundingClientRect()` to capture real element dimensions and positions, then rendering matching gray rectangles during loading states. The framework includes responsive breakpoint support and generates skeletons via a CLI build step that snapshots your running application.

repos.description: LLM Wiki is a cross-platform desktop application that turns your documents into an organized, interlinked knowledge base — automatically. repos.blurb: LLM Wiki is a cross-platform desktop application that automatically converts documents into an organized, interlinked knowledge base using LLM processing. Unlike traditional RAG systems that retrieve and process information for each query, it incrementally builds and maintains a persistent wiki structure that compiles knowledge once and keeps it current. The implementation is based on Andrej Karpathy's LLM Wiki methodology but extends it into a full desktop application with features like knowledge graphs, community detection, and web clipping.

The app uses a Cloudflare Worker proxy architecture to keep API keys secure while integrating with Anthropic's Claude, AssemblyAI, and ElevenLabs services.
